advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 ACL Bypass via Non-Canonical Plugin Paths
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.x before 2.7.2, and the openbao-plugins LDAP and RADIUS auth plugins before 0.2.0, contain an ACL bypass in the AppRole, Cert, LDAP, and RADIUS auth methods caused by implicit path canonicalization. Authenticated attackers can request non-canonical paths for AppRole Role IDs, Cert CRLs, LDAP groups and users, or RADIUS users to evade ACL deny rules.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 Wildcard Principals in SSH Certificates via Identity Templates
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.x before 2.7.2 does not neutralize wildcard characters in SSH certificate principals rendered from unvalidated external token metadata via identity templates in the SSH secrets engine. Attackers controlling that metadata, typically through a compromised identity provider, can inject '*' to obtain SSH certificates valid for multiple hosts or users.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 OIDC Provider Authentication Bypass via Client Credentials
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated callers to obtain OIDC ID tokens by abusing public clients with client_credentials enabled. Attackers who know a public client's client_id can request tokens from the identity/oidc/provider/<name>/token endpoint to impersonate the client without any secret.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 Path Traversal in Transit Key Import
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.5 and 2.7.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in Transit key import that allows authenticated attackers to bypass name restrictions in ACL policies. Attackers limited by a required_parameters name constraint can craft traversal sequences during import to write key material under arbitrary Transit key names.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 Improper Audit Logging of Root Generation and Rekey Responses
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.x before 2.7.1 fails to write response audit entries for the unauthenticated sys/generate-root, sys/rekey, and sys/rekey-recovery-key endpoints when request audit logging succeeds but response audit logging fails. An attacker using these endpoints can complete root token generation or rekey operations without a corresponding response audit record, hindering forensic detection.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 Expired AppRole SecretID Authentication Bypass
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.x before 2.7.1 does not check Secret ID expiration at use in the AppRole auth method, leaving expired Secret IDs valid until the periodic tidy removes them. An attacker holding an expired, untidied Secret ID can log in and gain access beyond its TTL.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 Role-Based Rate Limit Quota Bypass via Request Parsing
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.x before 2.7.1 contains a flaw in its rate limit quota subsystem where role resolution fails for requests with form-encoded bodies or forwarded certificates, so quota rules scoped to backend-specific roles are not enforced. Valid callers can repeatedly issue tokens without consuming the configured role-based rate limit budget.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 Kubernetes Auth Method Token Renewal After Revocation
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.4 and 2.7.x before 2.7.1 does not verify, when renewing a token issued by the Kubernetes Auth method, that the service account token originally used to authenticate is still valid. An authenticated attacker can keep renewing such tokens to persist access after the Kubernetes service account has been deleted.

advisories.title: OpenBao 2.2.0 before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 ACME EAB MAC Key Disclosure via Sanitized Configuration
advisories.summary: OpenBao 2.2.0 before 2.6.4 and 2.7.0 before 2.7.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that exposes the tls_acme_eab_mac_key value through the sys/config/state/sanitized endpoint. Callers of the sanitized configuration endpoint can retrieve the ACME External Account Binding MAC key used for TLS listener certificates, letting them bind to the operator's ACME account.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.3 Sensitive Data Leak in Audit Log via Malformed Parameters
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.3 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows attackers to leak sensitive data into audit logs by sending malformed plugin parameters. Attackers can submit requests with malformed TypeKVPair or TypeHeader field values, causing error messages containing sensitive input to be recorded in audit logs.

advisories.title: OpenBao 2.3.0 before 2.6.3 Missing Root Namespace Enforcement in Plugin Catalog APIs
advisories.summary: OpenBao from 2.3.0 before 2.6.3 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows privileged child-namespace tokens to modify plugin registrations because /v1/sys/plugins/catalog/* is not restricted to the root namespace. Attackers can remove existing registrations, create invalid ones, or register installed plugins through a child namespace's sys/ mount, causing denial of service.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.3 Missing Header Check on Agent/Proxy Quit Endpoints
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.3 contains a missing authorization check that allows attackers to stop Agent and Proxy services by omitting the X-Vault-Header. When require_request_header is enabled, attackers can send requests via server-side request forgery to /agent/v1/quit or /proxy/v1/quit to shut down these services.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.3 ACL Bypass via Dropped Templated Policy Denial
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.3 contains an ACL bypass vulnerability that silently drops explicit deny rules based on forbidden identity metadata templates within wildcard grants. Attackers whose identity metadata contains wildcard or path segments can access paths that should be denied within the broader wildcard-granted scope.

advisories.title: OpenBao before 2.6.3 Open Redirect via OIDC Identity Provider UI
advisories.summary: OpenBao before 2.6.3 contains an open redirect vulnerability in the UI's OIDC identity provider that affects users not authenticated to OpenBao. Attackers can craft OIDC links that redirect unauthenticated users to attacker-controlled destinations, enabling phishing or credential theft.

advisories.title: ACL Bypass via Non-Canonical URL Access in OpenBao
advisories.summary:
## Impact

Several locations within OpenBao allow access to resources via non-canonical names:

- Policies and workflows allow case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed, and path-simplified access to a tree of resources
- Certificate and Kubernetes authentication's roles, Userpass's user definitions, PKI seceret's `default` key and issuer references are case-insensitive.

When an ACL policy grants access via a broad wildcard and specific deny grants are used to exclude specific resources of the above types, an attacker can bypass the denial and access resources under the wildcard grant by using any of the names which do not match the explicit shape of the denial.

This vulnerability is original to HashiCorp Vault.

## Patch

This vulnerability is patched in OpenBao v2.7.0 and v2.6.3.

## Workarounds

Policy authors using this format of ACL policies would have to add grants for every single possible exclusion format, which may not be feasible depending on endpoint.

## Acknowledgements

@HarDToBelieve and @marcIlunga independently disclosed the vulnerability in the policy subsystem. @cipherboy expanded this to cover the remaining cases.

advisories.title: OpenBao 2.3.0 before 2.6.3 Incorrect Authorization via Policy Cache Namespace Traversal
advisories.summary: OpenBao from 2.3.0 before 2.6.3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in its ACL policy cache that allows tokens to reference policies from arbitrary namespaces using specially crafted policy names. Attackers holding such tokens can gain capabilities of cached policies in other namespaces, including the root namespace, to act across namespace boundaries.

advisories.title: OpenBao's PKI ACME Issues Certificate With Unvalidated SANs
advisories.summary:
## Impact

OpenBao's PKI engine supports the Automatic Certificate Management Environment (ACME - RFC 8555) protocol for certificate issuance. When enabled and configured by an operator, PKI did not correctly validate the certificate's SANs against the ACME protocol's completed orders, letting an attacker who can successfully validate for any allowed domain acquire a certificate also valid for any number of non-validated SANs. These SANs must be for a type non-issuable through the ACME protocol (e.g., email addresses).

This vulnerability is original to HashiCorp Vault.

## Patch

This vulnerability is patched in OpenBao v2.7.0 and v2.6.3.

advisories.title: Remote Code Execution via `sys/storage/raft/snapshot-force` Plugin Catalog Replacement in OpenBao
advisories.summary:
## Impact

In OpenBao, the `sys/storage/raft/snapshot` and `sys/storage/raft/snapshot-force` endpoint is a highly privileged endpoint to replace the current storage state, including the plugin catalog. The latter API allows replacement of storage state to a state unrelated to the current storage, without knowledge of the current seal mechanism.

OpenBao allows modification of the plugin catalog via API endpoint which is then stored within encrypted storage and thus are writable by the Snapshot APIs. When OpenBao is subsequently unsealed, plugins could be loaded and executed without conforming to the `plugin_directory` set in the server's configuration, allowing an attacker with write access to this endpoint to achieve remote code execution of arbitrary binaries on the underlying system. 

Operators not running the Raft storage backend are not affected.

This vulnerability is original to HashiCorp Vault.

## Patch

This vulnerability is patched in OpenBao v2.7.0 and v2.6.3.

advisories.title: OpenBao 2.5.0 before 2.6.2 PKI allowed_ip_sans_cidr Bypass via CSR IP SANs
advisories.summary: OpenBao from 2.5.0 before 2.6.2 fails to enforce the PKI role allowed_ip_sans_cidr restriction on IP SANs taken from a CSR when use_csr_sans is enabled. Authenticated callers with sign permission can submit a CSR with an out-of-range IP SAN to pki/sign/<role> and obtain CA-signed certificates for unauthorized IPs.

advisories.title: OpenBao - Internal Operation Dispatching Leads to Token Creation
advisories.summary:
### Impact

OpenBao's request handling mechanism did not validate operation type when non-HTTP API requests were created, such as with inline authentication and workflows. Certain internal operation types would result in token issues when handled as a login request. While these operations would by default not specify policies, identity entity resolution would still occur, potentially leading to attached policies on this token. All existing community-maintained plugins did not perform policy resolution on any internal operations and thus token scope would be limited.

### Patches

This has been patched in v2.6.2.

### References

Gia Bui (@yabeow) from Calif.io reported the inline auth problem and expanded impact was disclosed by @cipherboy.

advisories.title: OpenBao LIST ACL bypass: a trailing-slash LIST request skips a more-specific deny rule (unported Vault v2.0.3 fix)
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to 2.6.0, OpenBao's vault/policy/acl.go could evaluate a broader wildcard ACL grant before more-specific trailing-wildcard ACL paths with capabilities = ["deny"] for a LIST operation. When a parent path permitted LIST and a child path was denied, the trailing-slash lookup could therefore allow listing the denied path. Other operation types are outside the repository advisory's affected scope. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

advisories.title: OpenBao's Recovery Mode Vulnerable To Token Leakage via Timing Attack
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to 2.6.0, OpenBao's handleLogicalRecovery path in http/logical.go compared the highly privileged recovery token with ordinary string equality. A remote unauthenticated attacker able to make repeated recovery mode requests and measure response timing could infer the recovery token. The recovered token could then authorize recovery mode operations that read or modify OpenBao data. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

advisories.title: OpenBao's Templated Policies Allow Privilege Escalation via Wildcard Characters
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to 2.6.0, templated ACL, PKI, and SSH policies could substitute attacker-controlled identity data without rejecting syntax-significant characters. In ACL templated policies, asterisks, plus signs, and slashes could alter path matching. In PKI allowed_uri_sans_template and allowed_domains policies, an asterisk could broaden certificate issuance to unauthorized domains. In SSH allowed_users and allowed_domains policies, a comma could add unauthorized principals. Exploitation requires a deployment to use templated policy data that users can freely modify; templates based on the randomly generated identity.entity.id value are not affected. This could allow privilege escalation, unauthorized access, and unauthorized certificate issuance. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

advisories.title: OpenBao Agent Writes Secrets to Stdout
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to 2.6.0, OpenBao Agent's exec rendering mode could write secrets from env_template to standard output when command/agent/exec/exec.go re-created the template runner after repeated rendering failures, primarily after num_retries was reached. A process supervisor, log collector, or local user able to read that output could obtain the rendered secret values. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

advisories.title: OpenBao's System Backend allows Unauthorized Management of the containing Namespace
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to 2.5.5, OpenBao users granted capabilities on /sys/namespaces/root within a non-root namespace could exploit special handling of the literal root path in namespace canonicalization. The /sys/namespaces/* endpoint family can resolve its containing namespace through a path prefix or X-Vault-Namespace header. ACL checks occurred before root canonicalized to an empty path, causing /sys/namespaces/root to resolve to the system backend's containing namespace and allowing permitted lookups, deletion, locking, or custom metadata changes against that direct containing namespace. The root namespace and arbitrary unrelated namespaces are not affected, and available operations depend on the capabilities granted on the path and subpaths such as /api-lock. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.5.

advisories.title: OpenBao: Transit secrets engine crashes on key creation with `derived: true` for asymmetric key types
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to 2.5.5, an authenticated OpenBao caller with write access to transit/keys/* could terminate the server process by setting derived to true while the type parameter selected rsa-, ecdsa-, or ed25519. The Transit policy creation path in builtin/logical/transit/backend.go and sdk/helper/keysutil/policy.go could reach an error path that double-unlocked a mutex while handling this invalid asymmetric derived-key combination, causing a panic, no HTTP response, process exit, and denial of service. JSON and HCL key-creation requests can express the triggering combination. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.5.

advisories.title: OpenBao: Cross-namespace lease revocation/renewal via canonical sys/leases/{revoke,renew} - incomplete fix of CVE-2026-45808
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to 2.5.5, an OpenBao user with access to sys/leases/revoke/:lease_id in one namespace could revoke a lease in another namespace when the foreign lease_id was known, bypassing namespace ACL isolation. The affected lease lookup routing in vault/expiration.go allowed FetchLeaseInfo and loadEntry to resolve cached or stored lease data outside the request namespace, allowing a tenant that intentionally disclosed a lease identifier to have the lease and its underlying credential revoked by another tenant. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.5.

advisories.title: OpenBao: LDAPi ldaputil (wrong escape func)
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to 2.5.5, OpenBao used EscapeLDAPValue, an RFC 4514 distinguished-name escaping function, where RFC 4515 LDAP search-filter escaping was required in sdk/helper/ldaputil/client.go GetUserDN. With the LDAP authentication backend configured for an Active Directory UPNDomain path or UserDN and UserAttr binding, an attacker-controlled username containing filter metacharacters could alter the search predicate and select a different directory entry because EscapeLDAPValue does not neutralize the characters handled by ldap.EscapeFilter. A resulting token could be associated with another LDAP identity and gain access to secrets, policies, or modification capabilities assigned to that identity. This issue is fixed in version 2.5.5.

advisories.title: OpenBao's cross-namespace lease revocation via legacy sys/revoke path bypasses ACL
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to version 2.5.4, OpenBao's namespaces provide multi-tenant separation. A tenant who intentionally leaks lease identifiers can have their lease and underlying credential revoked or renewed by a user in another tenant via the legacy, undocumented `sys/revoke` and `sys/renew` endpoints. This is fixed in OpenBao v2.5.4.

advisories.title: OpenBao's Kerberos Auth Method Accumulates Unaccessible Tokens
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to version 2.5.4, in OpenBao's Kerberos auth method on the `GET` handler, or when an `Authorization: Negotiate` header is supplied, the response is includes a `logical.Auth` object in addition to an error message. This results in tokens being created with only the default policy, default TTL, and no entity information, which are hidden by the returned error message. No access to these tokens by the caller occurs and the authentication token is not ever made accessible outside of `sys/raw`. This is fixed in OpenBao v2.5.4. As a workaround, users may set a rate limit quota to limit the creation of these paths. As the path is unauthenticated, it isn't possible to deny access to it.

advisories.title: OpenBao's Inline Auth Incorrectly Redacted Headers
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to version 2.5.4, OpenBao's inline auth functionality incorrectly redacted audit log entries, resulting in non-auth headers being removed and auth-related headers being retained in cleartext. This requires an attacker to compromise access to the audit device. Operators should review leaked source authentication material and rotate it as appropriate. This is fixed in OpenBao v2.5.4.

advisories.title: OpenBao's Namespace Deletion May Not Delete Data Properly
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to 2.5.3, when OpenBao's initial namespace deletion fails, subsequent retries fail to properly remove all data before marking the namespace as deleted. This can affect any outstanding leases as well as potentially leaving unrelated storage entries around. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.5.3.

advisories.title: OpenBao has Decompression Bomb via Unbounded Copy in OCI Plugin Extraction (DoS)
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to version 2.5.3, `ExtractPluginFromImage()` in OpenBao's OCI plugin downloader extracts a plugin binary from a container image by streaming decompressed tar data via `io.Copy` with no upper bound on the number of bytes written. An attacker who controls or compromises the OCI registry referenced in the victim's configuration can serve a crafted image containing a decompression bomb that decompresses to an arbitrarily large file. The SHA256 integrity check occurs after the full file is written to disk, meaning the hash mismatch is detected only after the damage (disk exhaustion) has already occurred. This allow the attacker to replace **legit plugin image** with no need to change its signature. Version 2.5.3 contains a patch.

advisories.title: OpenBao allows SQL Injection in PostgreSQL database secrets engine
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to version 2.5.3, when OpenBao revoked privileges on a role in the PostgreSQL database secrets engine, OpenBao failed to use proper database quoting on schema names provided by PostgreSQL. This could lead to role revocation failures, or more rarely, SQL injection as the management user. This vulnerability was original from HashiCorp Vault. The vulnerability is addressed in v2.5.3. As a workaround, audit table schemas and ensure database users cannot create new schemas and grant privileges on them.

advisories.title: OpenBao's Certificate Authentication Allows Token Renewal With Different Certificate
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to version 2.5.3, OpenBao's Certificate authentication method, when a token renewal is requested and `disable_binding=true` is set, attempts to verify the current request's presented mTLS certificate matches the original. Token renewals for other authentication methods do not require any supplied login information. Due to incorrect matching, the certificate authentication method would allow renewal of tokens for which the attacker had a sibling certificate+key signed by the same CA, but which did not necessarily match the original role or the originally supplied certificate. This implies an attacker could still authenticate to OpenBao in a similar scope, however, token renewal implies that an attacker may be able to extend the lifetime of dynamic leases held by the original token. This attack requires knowledge of either the original token or its accessor. This vulnerability is original from HashiCorp Vault. This is addressed in v2.5.3. As a workaround, ensure privileged roles are tightly scoped to single certificates.

advisories.title: OpenBao's Token Store Allows Cross-Namespace Renewal, Revocation
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. OpenBao's namespaces provide multi-tenant separation. Prior to version 2.5.3, a tenant who leaks token accessors can have their token revoked or renewed by a privileged administrator in another tenant. This is addressed in v2.5.3.

advisories.title: OpenBao has Reflected XSS in its OIDC authentication error message
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to version 2.5.2, OpenBao installations that have an OIDC/JWT authentication method enabled and a role with `callback_mode=direct` configured are vulnerable to XSS via the  `error_description` parameter on the page for a failed authentication. This allows an attacker access to the token used in the Web UI by a victim. The `error_description` parameter has been replaced with a static error message in v2.5.2. The vulnerability can be mitigated by removing any roles with `callback_mode` set to `direct`.

advisories.title: OpenBao lacks user confirmation for OIDC direct callback mode
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to version 2.5.2, OpenBao does not prompt for user confirmation when logging in via JWT/OIDC and a role with `callback_mode` set to `direct`. This allows an attacker to start an authentication request and perform "remote phishing" by having the victim visit the URL and automatically log-in to the session of the attacker. Despite being based on the authorization code flow, the  `direct` mode calls back directly to the API and allows an attacker to poll for an OpenBao token until it is issued. Version 2.5.2 includes an additional confirmation screen for `direct` type logins that requires manual user interaction in order to finish the authentication. This issue can be worked around either by removing any roles with `callback_mode=direct` or enforcing confirmation for every session on the token issuer side for the Client ID used by OpenBao.

advisories.title: OpenBao Privileged Operator Identity Group Root Escalation
advisories.summary: OpenBao is an open source identity-based secrets management system. Prior to version 2.4.4, a privileged operator could use the identity group subsystem to add a root policy to a group identity group, escalating their or another user's permissions in the system. Specifically this is an issue when: an operator in the root namespace has access to identity/groups endpoints and an operator does not have policy access. Otherwise, an operator with policy access could create or modify an existing policy to grant root-equivalent permissions through the sudo capability. This issue has been patched in version 2.4.4.
